subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys that look like credentials be allowed into skill-owned host `exec` subprocesses, and how should that interact with generic exec secret stripping?
rationale: The current code violates the documented host skill-env behavior for real users, but a broad fix changes credential propagation into executable child processes and can conflict with the active generic-exec secret-leak hardening direction.

options.title: Allow only skill-scoped exec env
options.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for the skill's own host exec context while keeping dangerous env names blocked and stripping skill secrets from unrelated generic exec.

options.title: Require skill metadata declarations
options.body: Keep credential-shaped names blocked unless the skill manifest declares them, then update the `gog` skill or ClawHub package metadata and docs accordingly.

options.title: Keep current fail-closed behavior
options.body: Document that credential-shaped `skills.entries.<skill>.env` names are intentionally blocked and require top-level/system env or sandbox-specific env configuration.

recommendation.title: Allow only skill-scoped exec env
recommendation.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for the skill's own host exec context while keeping dangerous env names blocked and stripping skill secrets from unrelated generic exec.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses documented skills behavior, env security defaults, and credential-to-exec policy where steipete has the strongest recent history signal.
